builders.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
They did it. They made a Muse open weights model, which is a huge step forward for OSS in the US. 

This is going to further accelerate AI diffusion because enterprises will be able to mix and match frontier performance for orchestration and high end tasks, while being able to have low cost and tailored post trained models for repeatable workflows. 

Overall this dramatically increases token consumption and workloads across the stack. Great to see Meta doing this.

Moving from chatting back and forth with agents, to having agents that you spin up in the background to do useful work for you is probably on the order of 100X or 1000X more token consumption than what we’re seeing today. 

Most work right now is essentially rate limited by our ability to process and work with information. Moving data between systems. Reviewing a document. Looking through code for security issues. Processing log data to look for even patterns. Looking up information about a prospective client. Almost all of knowledge work is constrained by these steps, and AI has become a huge unlock to that. 

So our first step was to use AI to do these individual tasks much faster for us. That was the chatbot phenomenon that we have been experiencing for the past 3+ years. But we can still then only augment the work that we remain in the loop for, and we’re highly limited by our ability to parallelize this work by our own bandwidth and context.

But where we’re going is quite different. As AI models continue to improve at incredible rates, we can hand off more and more work to the agent. First it’s letting the agent run with a harder problem. Then it’s giving a few agents multiple parts of a task at once. But we’re not far off from being able to throw an arbitrary number of agents at a problem and just say “come back when you’ve accomplished this goal”. 

Now imagine that agent swarm for any problem we can think of. Protecting our codebases, data, and systems. QAing every change we make and make sure all our infrastructure is robust and does what it should. Looking through every document for potential risks. Auditing this company with vastly more data reviewed. And on and on. Most of this isn’t even replacing existing work we do, it’s all net new. 

These agents will get deployed as swarms by people, by workflows, by triggers, and by other agents. And none of this would be possible if the models weren’t getting better, and if the cost of AI didn’t make it affordable. Both of those trends though are playing out. Now the next frontier is just having enough compute. But this is where it’s heading.

StandX 不发币而选择补钱散场这件事，小编认为其实还是相对体面的。

理论上，有20万+用户和交易量，选择硬上 TGE 割一波，一些 Rug 和软跑路的项目就是这么做的。

但不发币，把剩余营收加上老板 @StandX_AG 出资，直接换成无锁仓的 DUSD 稳定币分给社区解散，这波“自掏腰包体面退场”已经算清流了。

只是苦了深度参与交互的撸毛党，原本博弈的是一个高估值的新币暴富机会，最终可能只有一笔回本性质的稳定币安慰奖。

不过看一眼链上数据，也能理解为什么团队选择主动刹车。

DefiLlama 数据显示，StandX 链上 TVL 在2500 万美元级别，

截至 10 月中旬：
-累计永续合约成交量高达惊人的 1450 亿美元，
-最近 30 天内也维持着约 110 亿美元的成交体量，
-在 89 个同类 DEX 中排名第 6，占约 4.2% 的市场份额。
-但未平仓合约量（Open Interest）只有1400万美元

放在一起看，高成交量、低持仓量、高资金周转率，这更像是典型的“刷量撸毛”盘面特征。

真正能留下的真实用户或许很少。本质上还是“积分预期驱动”的高周转刷量。一旦发币预期降温，资金和流动性都会快速干涸。

只是，如果连一个由前币安合约掌舵人带队、拥有两亿美金冷启动资金、产品体验高度成熟的 Perp DEX 平台，都无法将“积分大军”转化为真实的留存交易者，

那么市面上那些还在靠积分 PUA 用户、等着发币套现的同类竞品，它们底层的真实商业价值究竟还剩多少？

刷积分内卷的时代，可能真的过去了。

tweets.text:
One interesting irony is that computer science at Stanford started as a subdivision of the math department.

Now computer science has gotten so large that it’s acquiring math as a subdivision.

Similar to the military funding the Internet via DARPA, and now the Internet (via drones, robots, satellites, and the like) turning the military into a division of the Internet. All part of the network taking over functions from the state that gave it birth.

https://t.co/gyKDaMd3dg

Yes, AI is rapidly advancing mathematics (and theoretical physics problems that are essentially mathematical). Like Ramanujan’s notebooks, human mathematicians will spend months (years?) poring over the stream of papers that AI effortlessly generates, hoping to verify and understand them, probably until math itself (via Lean) becomes a branch of computer science like almost everything else.

However, after math and physics, there is still a next scientific frontier: chemistry, and especially biology and medicine.

I mean, it was already the frontier, but it’s the next one too. AI can crush deterministic math problems on the computer, but biomedicine is a highly empirical, noisy, multivariate, and yet often predictable domain.

Thus, AI radically increases our ambitions in biomedicine. All the omics data, all the messy literature, it can all be synthesized and analyzed in a flash. This is what the labs mean when they talk about curing all diseases. The tooling is available to take cracks at biomedical problems previously thought impossible.

Midjourney is doing this, Chan Zuckerberg is doing this, Anthropic is doing this, but there will be so much more.

AI will make virtual reality visually indistinguishable from physical reality.

Or: the metaverse is already here, it’s just not evenly distributed.

Or: what’ll people do if AI actually does take their jobs? Play amazing AI video games while robots do all the work. That future is also already here, and also not yet evenly distributed…
